thought.text: Found it: `runuser` received the whole ExecStart as a single quoted string. I need to split it into an array:

reasoning_content:
Two problems:
1. The previous failed attempt left a stale pidfile (`pid=3953` was dead, but the file was overwritten with 3984). Wait, looking at the trace: first `start_daemon` call (from the earlier failed oneshot) wrote pidfile 3953? No wait — the trace shows two invocations of `start qisutu-daemon.service`:
   - The first one (from the failed oneshot run at 14:13:08): `runuser: failed to execute ... No such file or directory` — hmm, that's a weird error. The setsid runuser command failed: "failed to execute /usr/bin/perl /opt/qisutu/bin/qisutu-daemon.pl". Wait, "No such file or directory" for the perl command? /usr/bin/perl does exist... Ah! The issue is: `runuser` spawns the command... hmm. Actually, the error "runuser: failed to execute /usr/bin/perl /opt/qisutu/bin/qisutu-daemon.pl --sleep 3 --max-jobs 100: No such file or directory" — this looks like runuser is treating the entire string as a single command path! In other words, quoting got broken somewhere: the argument to `--` became a single string instead of an argv array. Why? Because I'm calling it like this: `setsid runuser -u "$user" -g "$group" -- "$(sed ...)"`. Command substitution returns a single argument (the whole string). runuser -u q -g g -- "cmd string" → treats "cmd string" as a single argv[0] with spaces → no such file.

   Need to split into an array: use `eval` or bash array word splitting. Best: read the execstart string into an array with proper quote handling — for these simple ExecStart lines, word splitting is sufficient. Use `read -ra cmd <<< "$execstart"` and then `setsid runuser -u "$user" -g "$group" -- "${cmd[@]}"`.

   The first attempt's log also says "runuser: group does not exist" — was that from the earlier oneshot failure when group was empty? That was the pre-fix run (where f was the name 'qisutu-install-complete.service'... no wait, that was the sed error). Anyway, a stale artifact.

2. A stale pidfile was left behind from the failed start (3953, then 3984). Need cleanup: /run/qisutu/qisutu-daemon.pid.

Fix start_daemon:
```
local execstart=()
read -ra execstart <<< "$(sed -n 's/^ExecStart=//p' "$f")"
setsid runuser -u "$user" -g "$group" -- "${execstart[@]}" >>"$LOG" 2>&1 &
```
Also, if start fails, clean up the pidfile.

action.command: cd /usr/local/bin && grep -n "setsid runuser" systemctl && sed -i 's|    setsid runuser -u "$user" -g "$group" -- "$(sed -n '\''s/^ExecStart=//p'\'' "$f")" >>"$LOG" 2>&1 &|    local execstart=()\n    read -ra execstart <<< "$(sed -n '\''s/^ExecStart=//p'\'' "$f")"\n    setsid runuser -u "$user" -g "$group" -- "${execstart[@]}" >>"$LOG" 2>\&1 \&|' systemctl && grep -n -B2 -A2 "read -ra execstart" systemctl && bash -n systemctl && echo SYNTAX_OK; rm -f /run/qisutu/qisutu-daemon.pid
